question: If a ray of light is incident passing through the centre of curvature of a concave mirror, then the angle between the incident ray and the reflected ray will be equal to:
solution:
The correct answer is __**0∘**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• When a ray of light passes through the **centre of curvature of a concave mirror**, it travels along the radius of the spherical surface.
 
• The radius is perpendicular to the surface at the point of incidence, meaning the angle of incidence is **0°**.
 
• Since the angle of incidence is 0°, the reflected ray retraces the path of the incident ray, resulting in an angle between the incident and reflected rays of **0°**.
 
• This phenomenon occurs because the centre of curvature lies on the principal axis, and light striking it does not deviate from its path.
 
• Such behavior is a direct result of the **laws of reflection**, where the angle of incidence equals the angle of reflection.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Centre of Curvature**: The centre of curvature is the centre of the sphere from which the concave mirror is derived. It is denoted by the letter **C**.
 
• **Principal Axis**: The principal axis is an imaginary line passing through the pole and the centre of curvature of the mirror.
 
• **Law of Reflection**: States that the angle of incidence is always equal to the angle of reflection, measured with respect to the normal to the surface at the point of incidence.
 
• **Concave Mirror**: A concave mirror is a spherical mirror that reflects light inward and can form both real and virtual images depending on the position of the object.
 
• **Normal to the Surface**: A line perpendicular to the reflecting surface at the point of incidence, important for understanding the behavior of rays in optics.
